result.label: question
result.evidence: In src/api/health.ts, GET /api/v1/health returns HTTP 200 when status is "degraded" (when the queue depth exceeds 500, but db is up). The docs in docs/API.md state: "| GET | `/health` | `{ status, version, checks, queueDepth }`; 503 when the database is down". The code and docs specify that HTTP 200 is returned for both "ok" and "degraded" statuses, and 503 is only returned when down (db down). Thus load balancer probes looking for non-200 to remove instances from rotation will keep degraded instances in rotation unless configured to inspect the JSON body status for "degraded" / "ok" or check another endpoint.

Update `pickLocale` to parse quality values (q parameters) from the Accept-Language header parts, defaulting to `1.0` when absent, and sort the accepted locales by quality in descending order before matching against available locales.
